back: Distance of open water over which wind blows; with wind speed and duration it controls wave size.
Low, long, infrequent (about 6-8 a minute); strong swash, weak backwash; build wide gentle beaches.
High, steep, frequent (about 10-14 a minute); weak swash, strong backwash; erode and steepen beaches.
Bending of waves round headlands: energy concentrated on headlands, spread out in bays.
Swash up the beach at the angle of the waves; backwash straight down under gravity; sediment zigzags along the coast.
Weathering and mass movement (rockfall, slumping) acting on cliffs above the waves.
Friction with the sea bed slows the base; the crest outruns it, steepens and topples.
Sheltered bays, constructive waves, changes in coastline direction, river mouths, behind reefs or groynes.
